about.title: Personal Injury Help in Yorba Linda, California
about.longDescription: Yorba Linda is a quieter corner of Orange County, but its roads still see their share of collisions. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city logged 91 injury collisions that left 116 people hurt. No one died in traffic that year. Public-record counts show the heaviest volume along Yorba Linda Boulevard, Imperial Highway, Bastanchury Road, and La Palma Avenue, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the weekend commute builds. If you were one of those 116 people, or you were hurt some other way — a fall at a store, a dog bite on a neighborhood walk, a collision on your bike — you probably have questions about medical bills, lost wages, and what the other side's insurer is really offering. We handle personal injury claims throughout Yorba Linda and across Orange County. Our team works on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless your case ends in a recovery. California gives most injury claims two years to file, so reaching out sooner keeps more options open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Yorba Linda Claim

items.title: Two years is the usual window
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you were partly responsible, you can still recover — your share of the blame reduces the amount rather than eliminating it.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, distress, and loss of enjoyment of life. We can help document what the injury has actually cost you beyond the receipts.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: We work on contingency. We are paid only if your case results in a recovery, so you don't need savings to get representation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of injury. Claims against a government entity, such as a crash involving a city vehicle or a fall on public property, can require a written claim within six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it's wise to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly to blame does not prevent you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault but not eliminated. Insurers sometimes overstate a claimant's share, which is one reason people choose to have an attorney review the facts.
